headline: Graph and transformer models predict molecular associations and outcomes from omics data
label: Graph Learning Omics Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply graph neural networks and attention models to multi-omics, spatial, and single-cell data for prediction tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supervised deep learning over biological graphs and attention-based encoders that predict associations, binding relations, cell-type identities, and clinical outcomes from omics data. Graph neural networks and graph contrastive learning recur across lncRNA-disease and miRNA-disease prediction (TARLHN, SHiMDA), miRNA-mRNA binding (GIN-CRC-Pareto), RNA-to-protein prediction from spatial transcriptomics (DPAS-Graph), and multi-omics classification and prognosis (engGNN, BOMIFA, PathTransGCN). Transformer and foundation-style encoders appear in DNAmBERT, scRep, ST-ConMa, and Deconformer. The summaries emphasize architectural choices such as multi-graph fusion, Pareto-optimized multi-task losses, cross-attention, and mutual-information decoupling rather than newly reported biological mechanisms. Reported benchmarks include TARLHN's 10-fold CV AUC of 0.9638 and PathTransGCN's 87.6% accuracy on BRCA subtype classification.
